html:
Several days of rioting in Derry, Belfast and other towns of Northern Ireland in August 1969, when the British Army was sent in.

It began in Derry after an Apprentice Boys parade, with the "Battle of the Bogside" between Catholic residents and police. Nationalists in Belfast rose in support and loyalist crowds attacked Catholic streets. Houses were burned, and about 1,800 families, most of them Catholic, fled their homes. Eight people died.

British troops arrived on 14 August to keep the peace and were first welcomed in Catholic areas. Many Catholics felt the police had failed them, and some turned to a new kind of defence. That autumn the Provisional IRA was born from the split in the old IRA.

The riots mark the point where the Troubles became a conflict of armed groups, after the earlier civil rights marches.
sum: Several days of rioting in Derry, Belfast and other towns of Northern Ireland in August 1969, when the British Army was sent in.
